disease_label_per_paper: Trichinellosis with pyomyositis and secondary osteomyelitis
presentation_summary: A 12-year-old girl from the Indian Gangetic belt presented with three weeks of intermittent fever and right thigh pain.
Two days after fever onset she developed swelling and pain in the right distal thigh with painful restricted right-knee movement.
In the first week she had generalized myalgia and a transient patchy red rash over the thigh lasting about 6-8 hours.

She came from a low socioeconomic background, was non-vegetarian, occasionally consumed pork, and had eaten a hamburger within the prior month followed by four days of self-limited diarrhea, dyspepsia, and myalgia.
Examination found thigh tenderness with mild local warmth, painful restricted knee movement, and inguinal lymphadenopathy.
WBC was 13,700/mm3 with 10% eosinophils; blood cultures were sterile; Trichinella IgM serology was positive.

Ultrasound and MRI showed bulky heterogeneous deep thigh muscles, multiloculated fluid collection, acute distal femur osteomyelitis, large deep posterolateral thigh abscess, and adjacent muscle infiltration.

Muscle biopsy histology and pepsin digestion identified Trichinella larvae; she underwent drainage/debridement plus antibacterial therapy and mebendazole, with fever resolution over one week and no disease at six-month follow-up.

risk_context.source_text_value: Occasional pork consumption and hamburger in the prior month
Presented after fever and thigh pain since 3 weeks

observations.source_text_value: Fever documented not more than 101 F
Generalized myalgia in the initial week of fever
Episode of diarrhea after hamburger exposure
Patchy red rash over the front and medial thigh on day 2 lasting 6-8 hours
Tenderness and swelling in right distal thigh with mild local rise in temperature
Restricted movement of right knee due to pain
Palpation of inguinal lymph nodes revealed lymphadenopathy
IgM antibodies to Trichinella species were positive
No antibiotic treatment before admission and no anthelmintic therapy before diagnosis

imaging.finding: Grossly normal bony architecture with altered soft tissue shadows in surrounding thigh musculature.
Bulky heterogeneous deep muscles of the posterolateral mid and lower thigh with multiloculated fluid collection suggestive of myositis.
Signs of acute osteomyelitis of the lower femur with large abscess collection in the deep posterolateral thigh and adjacent muscle infiltration.

microbiology.result: Serous discharge with occasional pus cells; Gram stain, AFB, and culture sensitivity were negative.

diagnostics.result: Positive for IgM antibodies to Trichinella species.
Histology suggested parasitic infection with eosinophilic infiltrates; pepsin-digested muscle biopsy isolated Trichinella larvae.

clinical_course.event: Provisional diagnosis of acute osteomyelitis led to debridement and corticotomy; edematous bulky unhealthy muscle and minimal seropurulent discharge were found.
She received four weeks of intravenous cloxacillin with ceftriaxone after surgical drainage/debridement, followed by two additional weeks of oral cephalosporins.
Mebendazole was given orally in divided total dose 600 mg/day for 14 days.
General condition improved and fever subsided gradually over one week.
At six months she was disease-free without limitations in play or daily activities.

actual_treatment: Intravenous cloxacillin plus ceftriaxone for four weeks.
Oral cephalosporins for two additional weeks.
Oral mebendazole total 600 mg/day divided for 14 days.

outcome.source_text_value: Follow-up after 6 months showed the patient to be disease free with no complaints.

quality_warnings: The paper frames pyomyositis and osteomyelitis as unusual complications; they are preserved as complication evidence rather than used to rename the disease leaf.
Trichinella serology and biopsy are post-workup confirmation and marked non-ranking where mapped.
